'''Hikami Anego Shrine''' (氷上姉子神社) is a Shinto shrine located in Midori-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It is a Shikinaisha, and its historical Rank under the Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines was that of a Gōsha{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qid=Q134917316|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q712534}}. Currently, it serves as an external branch shrine of Atsuta Shrine.

The shrine is situated on a hill known as "Hikamiyama" (氷上山/火上山) and is said to be the site where the Kusanagi no Tsurugi, one of the Three Sacred Treasures, was enshrined before the founding of Atsuta Shrine. Locally, it is affectionately referred to as "O-Hikami-san."

== Enshrined Deities ==

The shrine venerates the following deity:<ref name="History_Pamphlet">Shrine history pamphlet.</ref>
* Miyazu-hime (Miyasu-hime/Miyazu-hime)

The deity is associated with the Owari clan, as indicated in texts such as the Nihon Shoki, Kojiki, and fragments of the Fudoki. The texts recount how Prince Yamato Takeru wed Miyazu-hime and entrusted her with the Kusanagi sword.

== History ==

=== Foundation ===

According to tradition recorded in the Atsuta Shrine's origin myths, Hikami Anego Shrine originated as the residence of Miyazu-hime, who safeguarded the Kusanagi sword before the establishment of Atsuta Shrine. It is said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Chūai and relocated to its current site during the reign of Empress Jitō.<ref name="History_Pamphlet"/>

=== Chronological Events ===

The shrine is listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō (927 AD) under the name "Hi-no-Kami Anego Shrine." Over centuries, the shrine was maintained and revered as a significant religious site connected to the Owari clan and Yamato Takeru legends.

== Architecture ==

The current main hall (honden) was relocated in 1893 from the Eight Swords Shrine, a subordinate shrine of Atsuta Shrine. Additional reconstruction and repairs were undertaken in 1986.

== Events ==

The shrine hosts several annual rituals:
* '''Grand Kagura Performance (March)''' - A traditional dance said to have originated at Atsuta Shrine.
* '''Ōdaka Festival (October)''' - Features parades with decorative floats and is a major local celebration.<ref name="History_Pamphlet"/>

== Access ==

* Address: Ōdaka-chō Hikamiyama 1-3, Midori-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture
* '''Transportation:'''
** 20-minute walk from Ōdaka Station on the JR Tōkaidō Line.
** 25-minute walk from Nawa Station (Aichi) on the Meitetsu Tokoname Line.
